blocks.heading: Proposed Theoretical Framework and Mechanism
blocks.text: This research plan introduces a candidate mechanism for massive neutron star formation by formally relaxing the static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state to incorporate rotational and thermal support from binary mass accretion. While existing observational constraints—such as the radius and mass bounds derived from GW170817—demonstrate the necessity of a sufficiently stiff equation of state to support massive remnants, standard static Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) limits remain contested by the population of millisecond pulsars exceeding 2.0 solar masses. The proposed framework unifies isolated spin-down and binary recycling pathways by modeling mass transfer as a continuous thermodynamic and mechanical perturbation. This modification predicts a distinct mass-spin relation, formalized as M = R(P), which differentiates binary-recycled massive neutron stars from isolated magnetic-dipole spin-down pulsars. The derivation is grounded in the assumption that companion ablation affects only the surface and magnetosphere, leaving the core governed by the relaxed effective equilibrium axioms.

blocks.heading: Verification Strategy and Boundary Conditions
blocks.text: The validity of the proposed mechanism is subject to strict boundary conditions, specifically the preservation of the causality bound (c_s <= c) and consistency with the observed population of massive millisecond pulsars. The research design prespecifies outcome branches that distinguish between support for the relaxed axioms and the sufficiency of standard rotational support models. A null or contradictory outcome would indicate that the relaxed static equilibrium axioms inevitably violate causality or tidal deformability constraints, or that standard stiff equations of state fully account for the mass-spin relation without requiring axiom relaxation. Consequently, the study advances a testable formal bridge between microphysical nucleosynthesis networks and macroscopic remnant properties, awaiting proof obligation verification to determine if the relaxed axioms can consistently produce observed massive neutron star masses within the defined validity domain.

claim_provenance.statement: Relaxing static equilibrium axioms of dense matter EoS with rotational/thermal support permits masses beyond static TOV without violating causality, predicting a distinct mass-spin relation for massive neutron stars.

The claim fails if the relaxed static equilibrium axioms violate the causality bound, or if the predicted mass-spin relation contradicts the observed population of massive millisecond pulsars, or if standard rotational support models fully explain the observations without needing the relaxed axioms.
